chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Bindar narrated that Abul-Abbas al-Himady quoted on the authority of Abu Ja'far al-Hazrami, on the authority of Hodbat ibn Khalid, on the authority of Homam ibn Yahya, on the authority of Qitadeh, on the authority of Aymen, on the authority of Abi Imamat that
God’s Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Blessed be those who believe in me without having seen me.' He then repeated it seven times.
ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of believing in the Prophet without having seen him?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records the Prophet’s assurance of paradise for those who believe in him without having witnessed him physically, a concept central to the faith of the later generations. The repetition of 'Tuba' (blessedness) seven times underscores the magnitude of this spiritual reward, bridging the gap between the eyewitnesses of the Prophet and the believers of all subsequent eras. This narration serves as a foundational proof for the validity of faith based on transmitted reports (tawatur) rather than direct visual encounter.
